headlines.title: Is ASML Holding (NasdaqGS:ASML) Still Undervalued After Its Recent Pullback?
headlines.summary: ASML Holding (NasdaqGS:ASML) drew fresh attention after CEO Christophe Fouquet tied executive pay to a new Workplace Experience Index that tracks employee morale, following a year of restructuring and planned cuts of about 1,700 management roles. Recent trading has been choppy for ASML Holding, with the share price falling 6.6% in the last session and down 16.1% over 30 days, even though the year to date share price return is 34.

headlines.title: Why Is ASML Holding (NasdaqGS:ASML) Tying Executive Pay To Employee Morale?
headlines.summary: ASML Holding (NasdaqGS:ASML) is tying CEO and executive pay to a new Workplace Experience Index focused on employee morale. The move follows internal data showing weaker staff engagement and recent job cuts across parts of the business. The Workplace Experience Index will influence compensation outcomes for senior leaders alongside existing financial and operational targets.

headlines.title: ASML (NasdaqGS:ASML) Stock Looks Fairly Valued On Its 149% Run
headlines.summary: ASML Holding has delivered a powerful multi year share price run. However, recent pullbacks and fresh headlines now put a sharper spotlight on whether its current valuation is really supported by its earnings power. With the stock still heavily influenced by expectations around chips for artificial intelligence, the key issue is how much of that earnings story is already embedded in today's price. Over the past 3 years the stock has gained 148.

headlines.title: ASML’s CEO is putting his paycheck on the line for employee morale. It could help retain talent that’s nearly impossible to replace
headlines.summary: After a year of layoffs and a drop in morale, Christophe Fouquet is betting that giving employees a say in what leaders earn will help ASML keep specialists who are costly to replace.

description: ASML Holding N.V. provides lithography solutions for the development, production, marketing, sales, upgrading, and servicing of advanced semiconductor equipment systems. The company offers lithography, metrology, and inspection systems. It also provides extreme ultraviolet lithography systems; and deep ultraviolet lithography systems comprising immersion and dry lithography systems solutions to manufacture various range of semiconductor nodes and technologies. In addition, the company offers metrology and inspection systems, including YieldStar optical metrology systems, a diffraction-based wafer metrology platform to assess the quality of patterns on the wafers; and HMI electron beam solutions to locate and analyze individual chip defects. Further, it provides computational lithography solutions, and lithography systems and control software solutions; and refurbishes and upgrades lithography systems, as well as offers customer support and related services. Additionally, the company offers hardware, software, and services to chipmakers to produce the patterns of integrated circuits. It operates in Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Taiwan, China, rest of Asia, the Netherlands, rest of Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the United States. The company was formerly known as ASM Lithography Holding N.V. and changed its name to ASML Holding N.V. in 2001. ASML Holding N.V. was founded in 1984 and is headquartered in Veldhoven, the Netherlands.
